title: Shim a mount to a set height
instruction: Stack shims flat on the black pad so the top of the stack is 80 mm above the pad, within 2 mm, using as few shims as possible. The purple, green, blue, red and white shims are 20, 25, 30, 35 and 45 mm thick.
context: Shimming sets a mount to its alignment height during spacecraft integration. The technician picks the fewest shims from a colour-coded kit whose thicknesses add up to the required height, since every extra layer adds play, and stacks them flat and centred. Unlike weighing out a target on a scale, where any pile on the pan reads the same, the total here has to be built as one level, centred stack on a 70 x 60 mm mount and read with a ruler. The instruction never says which shims to use, and no single shim reaches 80 mm. A 1 g tabletop analogue of integration bench work, done in Earth gravity; no microgravity is claimed.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = +0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed, black (sRGB 0.05, 0.05, 0.05): the mount pad, a plate 70 x 60 x 6 mm (along x, along y, tall) centred at (0.220, 0.305), straight out from the left arm's base, so it spans x 0.185 to 0.255 and y 0.275 to 0.335 and its top face is 6 mm above the table. Loose: five shims, rectangular blocks with the same 60 x 50 mm footprint, each standing flat on a 60 x 50 mm face with its 60 mm side pointing forward (along x), made of a 0.7 g/cm3 material so mass follows thickness: purple (sRGB 0.55, 0.25, 0.70), 20 mm thick, 42 g, centred at (0.330, 0.405); green (sRGB 0.20, 0.60, 0.25), 25 mm, 52.5 g, at (0.220, 0.405); blue (sRGB 0.15, 0.35, 0.80), 30 mm, 63 g, at (0.330, 0.205); red (sRGB 0.80, 0.12, 0.10), 35 mm, 73.5 g, at (0.220, 0.205); white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90), 45 mm, 94.5 g, at (0.330, 0.305). So the back row, 330 mm in front of the base line, holds blue, white and purple at 100 mm inboard, straight out and 100 mm outboard of the left arm's base, and the front row, 220 mm out, holds red, the pad and green in the same three lanes. Every shim is thinner than its footprint is wide. Neighbours in a row are 100 mm apart centre to centre (50 mm edge to edge), the rows 110 mm apart (50 mm edge to edge), and the pad's edges are 45 mm from the nearest shims. Nothing touches at the start. To build it: cut the shims from beech or maple (about 0.7 g/cm3), or print them to the stated sizes and masses, and paint them; tape a 6 mm black plate to the table at the stated position; mark each shim's footprint.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released the shims and moved clear, from a top photo, a side photo, a ruler and a small level. The stack is every shim that is off the table (its lowest point more than 3 mm above the table top) with any part of its outline, seen from above, over the pad's 70 x 60 mm outline; shims on the table, or off it and clear of the pad's outline, are ignored. The stack is valid when it holds at least one shim and every shim in it is at rest (under 10 mm/s), level (its thickness axis within 3 degrees of vertical, either face up, any yaw), centred (its centre within 15 mm of the pad's centre, horizontally) and resting on the surface under it: the lowest shim's lowest point within 2 mm of the pad's top face, every other shim's lowest point within 2 mm of the top face of the shim below it, and these gaps adding up to 2 mm or less. A shim on its edge or end, tilted, leaning on the stack from the pad, more than 15 mm off centre, still moving, or held, bridged or propped more than 2 mm above the surface under it spoils the stack. The height is read at the centre of the top shim's upper face, above the pad's top face. Score: 1.0 when the stack is valid, the height is within 2 mm of 80 mm and it uses two shims, the fewest that reach 80 mm (35 + 45); 0.75 when it is valid and within 2 mm of 80 mm with more shims (20 + 25 + 35); 0.5 within 7 mm with any number of shims (a set one 5 mm step off: 75 mm is 30 + 45 or 20 + 25 + 30, 85 mm is 20 + 30 + 35); 0.25 within 12 mm (two steps off: 70 mm is 25 + 45, 90 mm is 20 + 25 + 45 or 25 + 30 + 35); 0 for everything else, which includes no shim over the pad, a spoiled stack, any single shim (45 mm at most when flat), all five stacked (155 mm), and a correct set stacked beside the pad. Shims count in any order and either face up. The exact 2, 7 and 12 mm height limits and the 2 mm gap limits count (0.1 mm epsilon). Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 state held for 1 s. In simulation every test uses each shim's centre and quaternion, not its axis-aligned bounds. The pad is fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which the pad moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. In simulation release is inferred from rest, so a shim held motionless in its place on the stack would also count; on real arms the stack is read after the gripper has opened and moved clear.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the five shims back on their marks, flat with the 60 mm side pointing forward; the pad does not move.
fidelity: Approximate: real shims are thin plates chosen to hundredths of a millimetre; here they are blocks 20 to 45 mm thick so a top-down grip can lift them, stepping by 5 mm with a 2 mm tolerance, so the arithmetic and the level, centred stack carry over but fine measurement does not. Each colour's thickness is given in the instruction, as a colour-coded kit prints it. Nothing is clamped. One shared friction, matte colours, a fixed pad, Earth gravity.
